column1: # Profiles Tessera bundles, and where each one comes from.
# Tab-separated with `#` comments, because both the vendoring script and the
# application read this file and neither should need a parser library to do it.
# One description of the fact: what is expected here, what it is called, and
# under what terms it may be shipped.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   file      the name it is saved under in this directory
#   space     CMYK, RGB or Grey. Checked after downloading, so a URL that has
#             rotted into an HTML error page is caught rather than bundled
#   licence   a tag; the full terms are in LICENCES.md, which must have an entry
#   name      what to call it in the interface
#   source    where to fetch it
# NOTHING IS BUNDLED UNTIL `tools/vendor-profiles.py` HAS BEEN RUN, and nothing
# fetched is committed to this repository. The application offers whichever of
# these files is actually present, so a fresh checkout has a shorter list rather
# than a broken one.
# **`idealliance-crpc` may not be sold.** That is fine for a personal build and
# for Tessera's own free distribution, where the profiles are separate data files
# rather than part of the program. It is not fine for anybody selling Tessera or
# packaging it for a distribution that requires the freedom to sell — Debian's
# DFSG, for one. Those builds should run the script with `--skip idealliance-crpc`
# and offer the discovered system profiles instead.
# URLs rot. The script reports a fetch that fails and carries on with the rest;
# pass `--url` to give a moved file its new address, and please correct the row.
# See CANDIDATES.md for what else is worth adding, and HOW-OTHERS-SOLVE-IT.md for
# how Krita, Scribus, GIMP and darktable each handle this.
# --- The screen. Copy, distribute, embed, use and sell without restriction.
